name: AsyncAPI 3.0
registry_consequence: Async channel, operation and message contracts can be versioned separately from broker products.

name: Canonical ABI lift/lower
registry_consequence: Canonical lifting and lowering makes memory, encoding, ownership and cleanup boundary decisions inspectable.

name: cargo-auditable
registry_consequence: Embedding dependency metadata in binaries improves post-build attribution.

name: cargo-cyclonedx
registry_consequence: Cargo graphs can be exported as standardized SBOMs.

name: cargo-semver-checks
registry_consequence: Deterministic API-diff lints add evidence to, but do not replace, semantic compatibility review.

name: cargo-vet
registry_consequence: Distributed dependency audits allow review evidence to follow exact dependency versions.

name: CloudEvents 1.0.2
registry_consequence: A small event envelope standardizes occurrence metadata without owning domain payload meaning.

name: Component Model async ABI work
registry_consequence: Language-neutral tasks, streams, futures, backpressure and cancellation are modeled together.

name: WebAssembly Component Model
registry_consequence: Typed cross-language components separate interface contracts from core modules and hosts.

name: Component plus Strategy
registry_consequence: Replaceable components and configurable strategies generalize ports and adapters beyond a fixed application hexagon.

name: CycloneDX 1.7
registry_consequence: A lifecycle-aware BOM object model describes components, services, dependencies and attestations.

name: ISO/IEC/IEEE 42010:2022
registry_consequence: Architecture descriptions distinguish the entity from views, model kinds and conformance claims.

name: OpenAPI 3.1.1
registry_consequence: A language-neutral API description aligned with JSON Schema supports typed transport contracts while preserving semantic separation.

name: OpenSSF Scorecard
registry_consequence: Automated repository security signals create scoped evidence without claiming semantic conformance.

name: OSV schema
registry_consequence: Version-precise open vulnerability records support deterministic affected-range matching.

name: OpenTelemetry stable telemetry signals
registry_consequence: Portable trace, metric and log structures make runtime receipts less provider-specific.

name: Rust 2024 unsafe operation scoping
registry_consequence: Unsafe operations inside unsafe functions require explicit unsafe blocks, improving audit locality.

name: MSRV-aware Cargo resolution
registry_consequence: Dependency selection can consider rust-version instead of treating MSRV as prose only.

name: Secure Supply Chain Consumption Framework
registry_consequence: Dependency intake, inventory, update and incident processes are treated as a consumption lifecycle.

name: Sigstore keyless signing ecosystem
registry_consequence: Identity-bound signatures and transparency logs reduce reliance on long-lived signing keys.

name: SLSA 1.0
registry_consequence: Approved build provenance levels turned supply-chain assurances into verifiable producer and platform claims.

name: SLSA 1.2 Source Track
registry_consequence: Source history, review and source provenance become separately attestable from builds.

name: SPDX 3.0
registry_consequence: A profile-oriented BOM model covers builds, security, data and provenance beyond package lists.

name: WASI Preview 2
registry_consequence: Capability-oriented host interfaces make target requirements explicit.

name: WIT interface language
registry_consequence: A language-neutral interface contract can generate bindings without making generated code the semantic owner.

laws: A destination contract, normalized destination profile, activation mapping declaration, compiled mapping plan, source occurrence, effect proposal, authorization decision, execution attempt, provider receipt and business outcome are distinct identities.

laws: A correction, resolution, closure, consensus, adjudication, acceptance and recall are different occurrences and none erases prior evidence.
Adjudication is an attributable scoped judgment under external authority and retained reasons, defeaters and appeal; it is not a metric.
Agreement is metric-, population-, scale-, matching-, missingness- and design-specific evidence, never universal truth.
Assignment validates externally issued identity, competence and authority evidence but never issues them.
Completion of human work proves only a scoped submission occurrence; it does not prove correctness, review, consensus, adjudication or acceptance.
Consensus is the result of a declared combination rule; it neither erases dissent nor becomes adjudication or ground truth by arithmetic.
Consensus score is scoped evidence and never a probability of truth unless a qualified method contract explicitly defines it.
Input order cannot change an order-independent rule result; order-sensitive rules declare that fact.
Models and agents may propose assignments, findings, alignments, metrics, consensus candidates or reasons but cannot issue competence, waive conflicts, adjudicate, accept truth or authorize effects.
Potential owner, actual owner, performer, reviewer, adjudicator, approver and acceptance authority are distinct roles.

Task definition, task occurrence, assignment, lease, work attempt, submission, review issue, agreement estimate, consensus candidate, adjudication judgment and accepted artifact edition are distinct identities.

laws: A correction, resolution, closure, consensus, adjudication, acceptance and recall are different occurrences and none erases prior evidence.

Assignment validates externally issued identity, competence and authority evidence but never issues them.
Completion of human work proves only a scoped submission occurrence; it does not prove correctness, review, consensus, adjudication or acceptance.
Consensus is the result of a declared combination rule; it neither erases dissent nor becomes adjudication or ground truth by arithmetic.

Models and agents may propose assignments, findings, alignments, metrics, consensus candidates or reasons but cannot issue competence, waive conflicts, adjudicate, accept truth or authorize effects.
Potential owner, actual owner, performer, reviewer, adjudicator, approver and acceptance authority are distinct roles.

Task definition, task occurrence, assignment, lease, work attempt, submission, review issue, agreement estimate, consensus candidate, adjudication judgment and accepted artifact edition are distinct identities.

laws: A provider-native sequence is comparable only inside its declared writer, primary or partition epoch unless an independently proved order relation says otherwise.
A retried mutation with the same idempotency identity returns the same terminal outcome or enters reconciliation; an unknown outcome blocks blind repetition as a new mutation.
A stale expected source revision, index head, epoch or sequence yields a typed conflict and cannot overwrite a later admitted mutation.
A successful acknowledgement states only its exact admitted, journaled, committed and replica scope; it never implies search visibility or source-document acceptance.
Add, replace, delete and no-op are explicit operations. A provider implementation that realizes replace as delete-plus-add cannot silently weaken the selected batch or document atomicity contract.
Background segment merge or compaction may change physical representation but cannot create a source mutation, change logical mutation order or strengthen an acknowledgement.
Batch partiality is ordered and receipted per member; an all-or-none claim is permitted only for a provider profile that proves it at the declared scope.
Delete acknowledgement creates an editioned mutation/tombstone fact; verified disappearance requires a later visibility proof and explicit residuals for retained readers, replicas and caches.

Every mutation binds one stable index id and immutable index edition, stable document id, source revision reference, operation, writer/primary epoch, idempotency identity and expected-state precondition.
Flush, journal sync, stable commit, replication and visibility remain independently observable occurrences and may be ordered differently by different providers.
Identical frozen intent, precondition, epoch, policy and observed provider outcome produce the same canonical receipt and residual set.
Source document occurrence, projected index document, mutation intent, mutation attempt, acknowledgement, durable commit, search visibility cut and query result are distinct facts.

laws: A SearchVisibilityCut binds one immutable index edition, shard-topology edition, per-shard mutation frontier, reader/searcher snapshot identities, publication occurrence and explicit coverage/residual set.
A single scalar visibility token cannot claim a distributed cut unless it proves all targeted shard and replica frontiers represented by that token.
A visibility waiter returns success only when the exact required mutation frontier is observed in the declared target scope; timeout, cancellation or listener exhaustion is not visibility.
Already-running searches retain their bound point-in-time reader/searcher cut and are not retroactively changed by a later publication.
Background merges may replace segments while preserving the logical visible frontier; merge completion is not a new business mutation or visibility guarantee by itself.
Delete disappearance is proven only beyond the delete frontier for every required searchable cut, with retained-reader, replica and cache residuals explicit.
Identical mutation frontier, reader state, topology, policy, clock evidence and observations produce the same canonical visibility verdict and residuals.
Missing shards or replicas yield typed partial coverage, wait or refusal according to policy; they never silently become a complete visibility claim.
Mutation admission, mutation acknowledgement, journal durability, stable commit, refresh/reader publication and search visibility are non-collapsible occurrences.
Publication frequency, refresh listeners, waiting callers, retained readers, shards, receipts and deadlines are finite and refusal is explicit under exhaustion.
Read-your-writes is scoped to an exact mutation identity/frontier, index edition, target shard set and publication receipt; session proximity is not proof.
Refresh may make a mutation searchable without a stable index commit, while a durable commit may exist without the currently serving searcher seeing it; neither fact strengthens the other.
refusal_precedence: identity edition and authority failures precede semantic evaluation
invalid configuration precedes resource execution
resource exhaustion refuses rather than weakening the requested guarantee

bounds.time: finite deadline or operation-specific complexity bound; otherwise typed refusal

laws: A cursor is scoped by issuer, source occurrence, source object, purpose, edition, epoch and partition; differing scope is incomparable unless an explicit translator proves otherwise.
A paging token is not a CDC resume token, a snapshot cut is not a stream offset, and a source cursor is not a durable processing checkpoint.
Advance is monotone only inside one declared comparison domain and cannot cross an unresolved gap, expiry, reset or source epoch.
Cursor comparison is a partial operation whose incomparable outcome is data, never an exception silently replaced by ordering.
Observed source position, emitted record, durably stored checkpoint, acknowledged sink effect and source finality remain distinct facts.
Opaque payloads admit equality only; arithmetic or lexical ordering is forbidden unless the carrier profile defines it.
Reset creates a new epoch or explicit discontinuity; it never masquerades as ordinary advancement.
Translation never strengthens order, completeness, finality or replayability and records every loss or ambiguity as a residual.
refusal_precedence: identity edition and authority failures precede semantic evaluation
invalid configuration precedes resource execution
resource exhaustion refuses rather than weakening the requested guarantee

Selection methods, graph expansion, set operations, exclusion, kind filtering and indirect-test closure execute in declared precedence.
Unknown mutation completion requires reconciliation before retry; retry cannot convert ambiguity into success.
refusal_precedence: identity edition and authority failures precede semantic evaluation
invalid configuration precedes resource execution
resource exhaustion refuses rather than weakening the requested guarantee

boundaries.abi: No stable Rust ABI is implied; C ABI or WebAssembly Canonical ABI requires a separate versioned adapter contract.
boundaries.anti_corruption: Foreign DTOs cross a named ACL that declares mapping loss, validation, error translation and version compatibility.
boundaries.serialization: In-memory semantic types are not wire DTOs; each codec/schema is editioned independently.

bounds.state: caller-owned or explicit state-port capacity; no hidden durable state
bounds.time: finite deadline or operation-specific complexity bound; otherwise typed refusal

code_risk.ffi: isolated in adapter; validate layout, ownership, lengths, alignment, panic/unwind and callback lifetime
code_risk.generated: generator version, inputs and output digest recorded; generated code is never semantic authority
unsafe: unsafe forbidden in semantic core unless separately audited

differential_tests: compare independent implementations under identical typed decisions and budgets
model_tests: reference state machine or executable algebra
oracles: graph traversal and exclusion property tests
selection order and digest determinism tests
two independent implementations and cross-provider differential results
property_tests: laws and invariants over generated valid and invalid inputs

evolution.deprecation: announce replacement and last-supported editions; removal requires authority and migration evidence
evolution.migration: publish typed adapters, loss declaration, fixtures, rollback and evidence invalidation triggers

cancellation: bounded pure operations declare not_applicable; long work accepts cooperative cancellation
concurrency: ordering and parallelism are typed offer properties
execution.determinism: semantic result deterministic unless an explicit decision and receipt declare permitted nondeterminism

feature_laws: features do not select domain semantics
optional dependencies are activated only by additive features
conflicting features are refused

gaps.description: No two independent law-conformant implementation artifacts are bound in this registry.
gaps.resolution_condition: Bind at least two independently maintained implementations with passing scoped conformance receipts.

gaps.description: No implementation is qualified; two independent implementations and executed exact-scope conformance remain required.
gaps.resolution_condition: The semantic owner adjudicates the source gap and binds versioned evidence.

provider_requirements: bind an exact capability offer with current evidence
target_requirements: declare ABI, endianness, pointer width, atomic/thread, unwind and resource support where applicable

replacement.substitution_law: A substitute passes the same scoped semantic, failure, resource, effect and compatibility oracles without consumer knowledge of provider identity.

scope.boundary_rationale: Candidate boundary retained only because the source names an owner and a provider-independent contract; final cohesion and cycle review remain open.
scope.refusal_rule: Reject a split derived only from vocabulary count, package layout, vendor identity, deployment shape, or product packaging.
responsibilities: evaluate an explicit selector over one exact compiled manifest and form a deterministic dependency- and test-closed invocation set

supply_chain.advisory_policy: OSV/RustSec or ecosystem-equivalent scan is required for each released artifact and dependency closure.
supply_chain.provenance: SLSA provenance or equivalent attestation is required for qualified builds
supply_chain.reproducibility: build recipe, locked inputs, toolchain and environment are digest-bound; two-builder reproduction is an evidence tier
supply_chain.sbom: SPDX 3.0.1 or CycloneDX 1.7 bound to artifact digest

typed_inputs.default_law: No semantic default is inferred from provider, target, feature, environment or product name.
